meta.title: ZAWED | Cashless fuel for company fleets in Egypt
meta.description: ZAWED is an Egyptian platform for company fleet fuel: a prepaid wallet, an RFID tag on every vehicle, and every litre recorded the moment it is pumped.

hero.title: Every litre your fleet buys, on record the moment it's pumped.
hero.lead: Your company tops up one wallet. Drivers fuel with an RFID tag fixed to the vehicle, the station gets paid without cash, and you follow every fill-up from your own screen.

assurances.team: A team in Egypt, support in Egyptian Arabic
assurances.money: Accounts in EGP, to the piastre
assurances.offline: Fueling carries on when the internet drops

pos.description: An example fill-up with ZAWED: the station's POS reads the tag and checks the vehicle and the balance, the amount leaves the company wallet and is posted to the station, and the receipt prints.

phase.ready: Hold the POS to the tag

collage.description: An example fill-up seen in three places: the station's POS reads the tag and counts 40 litres, the company portal shows the new fill-up and the wallet balance goes down by its amount, and the receipt prints.

problem.title: Fuel goes out every day. The numbers arrive at the end of the month.
problem.lead: With the usual methods, days of paperwork and several pairs of hands sit between the litre pumped and the money paid.

cards.title: Fuel cards
cards.today: A card passes from driver to driver and car to car. Nothing ties it to one vehicle.
cards.withUs: An RFID tag bound to one vehicle. If it goes missing, report it in the portal and we block it.

cash.title: Cash and advances
cash.today: Drivers pay out of pocket or from a cash advance, and then the chase for receipts begins.
cash.withUs: Nobody carries cash. The money stays in the company wallet and is debited at the pump.

paper.title: Paper invoices
paper.today: Receipts get lost or are handwritten, and accounting adds them up by hand at month end.
paper.withUs: A receipt for every fill-up and a statement accurate to the piastre, ready to export any time.

fraud.title: Fraud
fraud.today: Extra litres on paper, or fuel that ends up in another vehicle entirely, found out after the money is gone.
fraud.withUs: Limits per vehicle, a cooldown between fills, and an alert when a fill exceeds the tank.

how.title: From top-up to receipt in three steps
how.lead: No app for drivers and no paperwork for accounting. Every step leaves a record you can go back to.

topUp.title: The company tops up
topUp.body: A bank transfer to ZAWED. Our team checks it, and two people approve it before the balance lands.

fuel.title: The driver fuels with the tag
fuel.body: The attendant holds the POS to the tag. It checks the vehicle, its limits and the balance before any fuel flows.

record.title: Every litre is recorded
record.body: The amount leaves the wallet as a double-entry posting, the driver gets a receipt, and the fill-up shows on your screen straight away.

fleets.title: For fleet owners: you set the rules for each vehicle
fleets.lead: Decide when each vehicle can fuel, how much, and which grade. ZAWED enforces it at the pump.

limits.title: Per-vehicle limits
limits.body: In litres or pounds, per day, week or month, with the fuel grade the vehicle may take.

cooldown.title: Cooldown between fills
cooldown.body: A tag can't fuel again before the time you set, even at a different station.

departments.title: Departments and branches
departments.body: Group vehicles by department and follow each department's fill-ups on their own.

alerts.title: Alerts when they matter
alerts.body: When the wallet runs low, or a fill-up goes past the vehicle's tank capacity.

statements.title: Statements to the piastre
statements.body: Every fill-up with its date, station, vehicle and volume, ready to export for your accountant.

lostTag.title: Lost a tag?
lostTag.body: Report it in the company portal. We block the tag and bind a new one to the same vehicle.

card.label: Example vehicle in the company portal

stations.title: For station owners: every litre you sell is paid for before it's pumped
stations.lead: Companies prepay into their wallet, so a fill-up only goes through when the balance covers it. No credit terms and no collection calls.

paid.title: Your money is secured up front
paid.body: With every fill-up the amount moves to your payable balance, and you can watch it grow in the station portal.

payouts.title: Payouts from your payable
payouts.body: Transfers go from your payable balance to your bank account, approved by two people on our team.

cash.title: No cash in the drawer
cash.body: Fleet customers don't pay cash, so there's nothing to count and no shortfall at the end of a shift.

pos.title: A POS, set up for you
pos.body: We register and activate the device for your station, and every attendant gets their own PIN.

offline.title: Works without internet
offline.body: If the connection drops the POS keeps going, and sends the fill-ups once it's back.

shifts.title: Clear shifts
shifts.body: Each shift with its attendant, device and fill-ups, laid out in the station portal.

trust.title: How we keep the money and the data safe
trust.lead: Every pound follows the same path, and each step has a check the system runs on its own. You can watch it happen in a demo.

realtime.title: Each litre recorded as it's pumped
realtime.body: A fill-up is posted the moment it happens. One made while offline is posted as soon as the POS reconnects.

piastre.title: Accurate to the piastre
piastre.body: Money is counted in whole piastres, so no rounding differences pile up by month end.

limits.title: Limits and cooldowns
limits.body: The station's POS checks them before any fuel flows, even while offline.

isolation.title: Each company's data kept apart
isolation.body: The database itself stops one company from reaching another company's data.

path.caption: The money path: the company's bank transfer becomes wallet balance after two people approve it; each fill-up moves money from the wallet to the station's payable as a balanced ledger entry, online or offline; the station's payout goes to its bank after two people approve it; every step is written to an audit log.

gates.pump: A balanced ledger entry at the pump, even offline

path.audit: Each step goes into an audit log that records who did it and when, and the log itself can't be edited.

egypt.title: Made in Egypt, around how business works here
egypt.lead: We're an Egyptian team, and we built ZAWED around the way companies and stations in Egypt actually work.
egypt.clock: The time in Cairo right now

egp.title: In Egyptian pounds
egp.body: Prices, balances and statements in EGP, down to the piastre.

time.title: On Cairo time
time.body: Every fill-up and statement is stamped in Cairo time, with no time-zone sums.

arabic.title: Arabic first
arabic.body: The interface is built in Arabic from the start, with English alongside. Plates appear exactly as on the licence.

support.title: Support in Egyptian Arabic
support.body: You talk to people who know the business, on WhatsApp or e-mail, in Egyptian Arabic or English.

invoice.title: E-invoicing
invoice.body: Today you get a monthly statement of every fill-up. Connecting to the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-invoice system is next on our roadmap.

pilot.title: We're starting with a small group of fleets and stations
pilot.lead: ZAWED is getting ready for its first pilot in Egypt. Fleets and stations that join run the full system on their own vehicles and pumps, with our team beside them from day one.

setup.title: Set-up with our team
setup.body: We register your vehicles, fit the tags and train the people who will use the portal and the POS.

feedback.title: A direct line to the people building it
feedback.body: Tell us what gets in your way, and talk to the team that can change it.

terms.title: Terms agreed before you start
terms.body: We agree the pilot's length, scope and price with you in writing before anything goes live.

pricing.title: Plans sized to your fleet
pricing.lead: Priced per vehicle per month, and lower as your fleet grows. Every plan includes every feature.
pricing.notice: These prices are indicative. We agree the final price after a call about what you need.
pricing.yearlyHint: A year for the price of {{months}} months
pricing.customHint: Based on fleet size and your routes

included.portal: Company portal for all your users
included.support: Support on WhatsApp in Egyptian Arabic

pricing.stationsNote: For stations: joining terms are agreed with each station.

app.q: Does the driver need a phone or an app?
app.a: No. The tag is fixed to the vehicle, and the station attendant uses the POS.

offline.q: If the station loses internet, does fueling stop?
offline.a: No. The POS carries on under the same limits and sends the fill-ups once it reconnects. If anything conflicts, our team gets an alert.

topUp.q: How do we top up the wallet?
topUp.a: By bank transfer to ZAWED's account; then you send the transfer details from the company portal. Our team checks it, and the balance lands after two people approve.

otherCar.q: What stops a driver fueling another car?
otherCar.a: The tag is bound to one vehicle, with that vehicle's limits and cooldown. A fill-up larger than the tank raises an alert.

where.a: At ZAWED partner stations. We're signing stations ahead of the pilot, so tell us your vehicles' routes and we'll plan around them.

invoice.a: Today you get a monthly statement of every fill-up. Connecting to the e-invoice system is on our roadmap, and we'll let you know when it's ready.

data.a: Each company's data is isolated in the database itself, and every change records who made it and when.

stationPay.q: How does a station get paid?
stationPay.a: Each fill-up adds to the station's payable balance. Payouts go from that balance to the station's bank account after two people on our team approve.

try.q: Can we try it before we sign up?
try.a: Request a demo and we'll show you the system running on sample data, then talk about a pilot on your fleet.

demo.title: Let us show you ZAWED on your fleet
demo.lead: Leave your details and we'll call to set a time. In a hurry? Message us on WhatsApp.
